LONGER NOTE ON JEREMIAH: Chapters 42-44.

"The Jews which dwell in the land op Egypt " (Jeremiah 44:1 ).

As the end of the kingdom of Judah drew near, many of the Jews were determined to go into Egypt ; and this in spite of the warning given by Jehovah through Jeremiah. In Jeremiah 44 we have the latest prophecy concerning those who had gone thither; which declared that they should not escape, but should be consumed there (Jeremiah 44:27 , &c). This prophecy must have been fulfilled concerning that generation; but their successors, or others that subsequently followed, continued there a little longer, until the time came for Egypt itself to fall into the hands of Babylon. Recent discoveries of Papyri in the ruins of Elephantine (an island in the Nile, opposite Assouan), dating from the fifth century BC, bear witness to two great facts:

(1) That Jews were then dwelling there (in 424-405 BC).

(2) That they were observing the Feast of the Passover, "as it is written in the law of Moses".

The importance of these Papyri lies in the fact that modern critics confidently assert and assume that the greater part of the Pentateuch was not written till after the Exile ; and even then neither collectively as a whole, nor separately in its distinctive books.

In App-92 . it is shown that all through the prophets (who lived at the time of the kings in whose reigns they prophesied) there is a constant reference to the books of the Pentateuch, which conclusively proves that their contents were well known both to the prophets themselves and those whom they addressed. The Pentateuch, being full of legal expressions, technical ceremonial terms, and distinctive phraseology, affords abundant evidence of the above fact, and makes it easy to call continuous attention to it in the notes of The Companion Bible.

But there is further evidence found in the Papyri now discovered in the ruins at Elephantine in Upper Egypt.

They show that the Jews who dwelt there had a temple of their own and offered up sacrifices therein. That once, when this their temple was destroyed by the Egyptians, they appealed to the Persian governor of Judah, asking permission to restore it (Papyrus I).

There is a list preserved, registering the contributions towards the upkeep of the temple (containing the names of many ladies).

But the most interesting and important of these Papyri is one dated in the year 419 BC which is a Passover "announcement" of the approaching feast, such as were made from the earliest times to the present day (see Nehemiah 8:15 ), containing a brief epitome of its laws and requirements. This particular announcement shows that the following passages were well known : Exodus 12:16 . Leviticus 23:7-8 . Numbers 9:1-14 .Deuteronomy 16:6 .

This Papyrus has been recently published by Professor Edward Sachau, of Berlin: Aramdische Papyrus una Ostraka aus einer jildischen Militarkolonie zu Elephantine. Altorientalische Sprachdenkmaler des 5. Jahrhunderts vor Chr., mit 75 Lichtdrucktafalein. Leipzig, 1911. A small edition (texts only) by Professor Ungnad, of Jena, is published also under the title of Aramaische Papyrus aus Elephantine.

Nearly 2,400 years, since this announcement by Hananjah to the Jews in Egypt, have gone by. Elephantine is now a heap of ruins. The colony of Jews has passed away (unless the "Falashas" of Abyssinia are their descendants), but the Jewish nation still exists, and continues to keep the Passover, a standing witness to their truth of holy Scripture.

entries.content: But. Supply the Ellipsis thus: But [not so I], for I have laid Esau bare, &c.

entries.title: children
entries.content:
children = young children. Not the same word as in Jeremiah 49:6 .

trust = confide. Hebrew. batah . App-69 .

entries.title: the cup.
entries.content: the cup. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Subject), for its contents. See Jeremiah 25:15 .

entries.title: I have sworn.
entries.content:
I have sworn. Reference to Pentateuch (Genesis 22:16 ). App-92 .

Bozrah. Now el Buseirah, south-east of the Dead Sea. Not the Bozrah of Jeremiah 48:24 .

entries.title: heathen
entries.content:
heathen = nations.

ye together =. yourselves out [to war].

entries.title: men.
entries.content: men. Hebrew. 'adam (with Art.) App-14 .

entries.title: terribleness
entries.content:
terribleness = monstrous thing: i.e. an Edomite Asherah. App-42 .

pride = insolence.

the rock. Probably Sela.

nest. Compare Obadiah 1:4 .

eagle = vulture.

entries.title: a desolation
entries.content: a desolation = an astonishment.

entries.title: the overthrow, &c.
entries.content: the overthrow, &c. Reference to Pentateuch (Genesis 19:25 .Deuteronomy 29:23; Deuteronomy 29:23 ). App-92 . A word almost restricted to that event.

entries.title: he.
entries.content:
he. Nebuchadnezzar. See note on Jeremiah 48:40 .

like a lion. Figure of speech Simile. Contrast Jeremiah 4:7 , where the assault is against Zion and the feelings are more deeply stirred.

swelling. Hebrew pride. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), for the proud beasts in the undergrowth of its banks. See Jeremiah 12:5 ; Jeremiah 50:44 . Compare Job 41 .

the strong = a strong one.

but = for.

him: i.e. Edom.

from her: i.e. from Idumea.

a chosen man: i.e. Nebuchadnezzar.

over her = over the pasturage.

who is like Me? Compare note on Exodus 15:11 .

appoint Me the time? i.e. who will summon or arraign Me?

shepherd = ruler.

entries.title: counsel.
entries.content:
counsel. Referring to Teman's wisdom. Compare Jeremiah 49:7 .

taken = counselled. Figure of speech Polyptoton.

draw them out. As a dog drags away and tears a dead body.

habitations: or, folds.

entries.title: the noise thereof.
entries.content:
the noise thereof. Hebrew = its sound. Some codices, with eight early printed editions and Aramaean, read "at their noise" (plural)

in = at.

entries.title: fly as the eagle.
entries.content:
fly as the eagle. Reference to Pentateuch (Deuteronomy 28:49 ). App-92 . Compare Jeremiah 48:40 .

mighty men. Hebrew. geber. App-14 .

entries.title: The Forty-Seventh Prophecy of Jeremiah
entries.content:
The Forty-Seventh Prophecy of Jeremiah (see book comments for Jeremiah).

Damascus. The prophecy concerns Syria generally, of which Damascus was the principal city.

Hamath. Now Hama, in the valley of the Greekntes, north of Damascus.

Arpad. Now Tell Erfad, thirteen miles north of Aleppo. Compare 2 Kings 18:34 ; 2 Kings 19:13 .Isaiah 10:9 ; Isaiah 36:19 ; Isaiah 37:13 .

evil tidings = calamitous report. Hebrew. ra'a' . App-44 .

sorrow = anxiety, or trouble. Hebrew. ra'a'. App-44 . Not the same word as in Jeremiah 49:24 . be quiet = rest.

entries.title: sorrows
entries.content: sorrows = pangs. Hebrew. hebel, as in Jeremiah 13:21 .

entries.title: not left
entries.content: not left = not restored, strengthened, or fortified. A Homonym. Here the meaning is as in Nehemiah 3:8 . See notes on Exodus 23:5 . Deu 32:36 . 1 Kings 14:10 . 2 Kings 14:26 . 2Ki 49:25 . Not its other meaning, to leave or forsake, as in Genesis 2:24 ; Genesis 39:6 . Nehemiah 5:10 . Psalms 49:10 . Mai. Jeremiah 4:1 (Hebrew = Ch. Jeremiah 3:19 ).

entries.title: men.
entries.content: men. Hebrew, plural of' 'enosh . App-14 .

entries.title: Ben-hadad.
entries.content: Ben-hadad. Three kings of Damascus bore this official name. See 1Ki 15:18 . 2 Kings 13:3 , 2 Kings 13:25 .

entries.title: The Forty-Eighth Prophecy of Jeremiah
entries.content:
The Forty-Eighth Prophecy of Jeremiah (see book comments for Jeremiah).

Kedar. Name of the Bedouin dwelling in tents (Jeremiah 2:10 ), east of Palestine.

Hazor. Near the Euphrates and the Persian Gulf.

men = sons.

entries.title: Fear is on every side.
entries.content: Fear is on every side. Hebrew. magor missabib. Compare Jeremiah 6:25 ; Jeremiah 20:3 , Jeremiah 20:10 ; Jeremiah 46:5 .Lamentations 2:22 .

entries.title: conceived a purpose
entries.content: conceived a purpose = devised a device. Figure of speech Polyptoton.

entries.title: which dwell alone.
entries.content: which dwell alone. Reference to Pentateuch (Numbers 23:9 . Deuteronomy 33:28 ).

entries.title: all winds
entries.content:
all winds = all quarters. winds. Hebrew. ruach. App-9 .

in the utmost corners = have the corners of their hair or beards polled. Compare Jeremiah 9:26 .

entries.title: dragons
entries.content: dragons = jackals.

entries.title: The Forty-Ninth Prophecy of Jeremiah
entries.content:
The Forty-Ninth Prophecy of Jeremiah (see book comments for Jeremiah).

Elam. The country east of the Tigris. Compare Daniel 8:1 , Daniel 8:2 . Its subjugation by Nebuchadnezzar (Jeremiah 25:25 ). Compare Habakkuk 2:8 .

entries.title: four.
entries.content: four. The number connected with the earth ( App-10 ).

entries.title: life
entries.content: life = soul. Hebrew. nephesh. App-13 .

entries.title: the latter days.
entries.content:
the latter days. The end or after part of the days.

bring again, &c. See note on Jeremiah 48:47 . Compare Deuteronomy 30:3 .

entries.title: The Fiftieth Prophecy of Jeremiah
entries.content:
The Fiftieth Prophecy of Jeremiah (see book comments for Jeremiah).

the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah . App-4 .

and. Some codices, with three early printed editions, Aramaean, Syriac, and Vulgate, read this "and" in the text.

by. Hebrew idiom = by the hand of; "hand" being put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Cause), for the instrumentality or agency, especially in the inspiration of the written words. See note on Zechariah 7:12 .

entries.title: publish . . . conceal not.
entries.content:
publish . . . conceal not. Not now using symbols as in Jeremiah 25:15 .

set up = lift up.

Babylon is taken. Compare Revelation 14:8 ; Revelation 18:6 , Revelation 18:10 , Revelation 18:21 : showing that this prophecy is still future.

Bel. Contracted from the Aramaic form of Ba'al , the national god of Babylon. See Isaiah 46:1 .

Merodaoh. Another name for Bel (= Baal), Babylon ' s god.

images = manufactured gods. Compare Leviticus 26:30 .

entries.title: the north.
entries.content:
the north. Referring to Medo-Persia, which was on the northwest of Chaldea. But a future enemy is foretold.

none shall dwell therein. Showing that the fulfilment is still future.

entries.title: In those days.
entries.content:
In those days. This prophecy awaits its fulfilment. The conquest by Medo-Persia did not exhaust it.

children = sons.

together. Another proof that this prophecy refers to the future. Never yet fulfilled.

going and weeping. Hebrew = weeping as they travel, so shall they journey on.

weeping. For their past sins. Compare Jeremiah 31:9 , Jeremiah 31:18 . Joel 2:12 .Zechariah 12:10-14 .Revelation 1:7 .

the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. (with ' eth). App-4 .

God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

entries.title: thitherward.
entries.content:
thitherward. Hebrew = hitherward. Jeremiah was therefore not in Babylon, but in Egypt.

perpetual. Another evidence that this prophecy refers to the future covenant. Compare Jeremiah 3:18 Jeremiah 4:2 ; Jeremiah 11:1-6 ; Jeremiah 31:31 .

entries.title: lost sheep.
entries.content:
lost sheep. Compare Matthew 10:6 ; Matthew 15:24 .

shepherds: i.e. rulers.

they have turned them away on the mountains = on the mountains they seduced them: i.e. by the idolatrous worship practiced there.

entries.title: We offend not, &c.
entries.content:
We offend not, &c. Compare verses: Jeremiah 50:15 , Jeremiah 50:23 , Jeremiah 50:29 ; Jeremiah 2:3 ; Jeremiah 25:14 , Jeremiah 25:15 , &c.

offend. Hebrew. 'asham. App-44 .

sinned. Hebrew. chata.

Habitation = pasturage. Compare Jeremiah 31:23 .

justice = righteousness. In Ch. Jeremiah 31:23 this is applied to Jerusalem. Here Jehovah Himself is the pasturage in which His People find rest.

the Hope of their fathers. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), App-6 , by which "hope" is put for the God in Whom their fathers hoped. Compare 1 Timothy 1:1 .

entries.title: go forth.
entries.content: go forth. Hebrew text reads "they will go forth"; but margin, with some codices and two early printed editions, reads "go ye forth". Compare Jeremiah 51:4 , Jeremiah 51:6 . Revelation 18:4 .

entries.title: assembly
entries.content:
assembly = a gathered host, or convocation. great nations. Compare Isaiah 13:3 , Isaiah 13:4 .

mighty . . . man. Hebrew. gibbor. App-14 .

expert = successful. Compare Jeremiah 10:21 ; Jeremiah 23:5 .

entries.title: shall be satisfied.
entries.content: shall be satisfied. Compare Jeremiah 49:9 .

entries.title: destroyers
entries.content: destroyers = spoilers, or plunderers.

entries.title: the hindermost
entries.content: the hindermost = the last. Compare Jeremiah 50:17 ; Jeremiah 25:26 .

entries.title: not be inhabited.
entries.content: not be inhabited. Not yet fulfilled. Compare 1 Peter 5:13 .

entries.title: given her hand.
entries.content:
given her hand. Put by Figure of speech Metonymy (of Adjunct), App-6 , for what is done by it. Here the token of submission. Compare Lamentations 5:6 . Ezekiel 17:18 .

as = according as. Compare Revelation 18:6 , Revelation 18:7 .

entries.title: every one.
entries.content: every one. Hebrew. 'ish. App-14 .

entries.title: Israel.
entries.content:
Israel. Now a united nation. See note on Jeremiah 50:4 .

last. See note on "hindermost", Jeremiah 50:12 .

entries.title: the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel.
entries.content: the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel. See note on Jeremiah 7:3 .

entries.title: mount
entries.content: mount = the hill country of.

entries.title: Merathaim
entries.content:
Merathaim = double rebellion. So called, here, because the empire was founded in a double rebellion.

Pekod = Visitation: i.e. in judgment.

destroy = devote to extermination. Hebrew. karam. The same word as Jeremiah 50:26 ; not the same as verses: Jeremiah 50:11 , Jeremiah 50:22 .

entries.title: destruction
entries.content: destruction = smash; or, breaking down. Hebrew. shabar. Not the same word as in verses: Jeremiah 50:11 , Jeremiah 50:21 , Jeremiah 50:26 .

entries.title: His armoury.
entries.content: His armoury. Figure of speech Anthropopatheia.

entries.title: from the utmost border
entries.content: from the utmost border = from the farthest parts, or every quarter.

entries.title: visitation.
entries.content: visitation. See note on "Pekod", Jeremiah 50:21 .

entries.title: vengeance
entries.content: vengeance = avenging. Son 51:11 . Compare Daniel 5:3 .

entries.title: recompense her.
entries.content:
recompense her. See Revelation 18:6 .

according to. See note on "as", Jeremiah 50:15 . Compare Revelation 18:6 .

the Holy One of Israel. See note on Psalms 71:22 .

entries.title: Redeemer
entries.content:
Redeemer = Kinsman-Redeemer. Hebrew. ga'al. See notes on Isaiah 60:16 , and Exodus 6:6 .

strong = strong (to hold fast). Hebrew. hazak. Not the same word as in Jeremiah 50:44 .

entries.title: A sword.
entries.content: A sword. Note the Figure of speech Anaphora, in five successive sentences.

entries.title: liars
entries.content:
liars = praters.

dote = be shown to be foolish.

entries.title: the mingled people
entries.content: the mingled people = the rabble.

entries.title: idols
entries.content: idols = horrors.

entries.title: no more inhabited, &c.
entries.content: no more inhabited, &c. Therefore the fulfilment still future.

entries.title: overthrew, &c.
entries.content:
overthrew, &c. Reference to Pentateuch (Genesis 19:25 ). App-92 . Compare Jeremiah 49:18 .

man. Hebrew ' Ish . App-14 .

entries.title: a great nation:
entries.content:
a great nation: i.e. Medo-Persia.

coasts = sides: i.e. remote parts.

entries.title: his hands, &c.
entries.content: his hands, &c. See fulfilment in Daniel 5:6 .

entries.title: like a lion, &c.
entries.content: like a lion, &c. See note on Jeremiah 49:19 for this verse and Jeremiah 50:45 , there spoken of Edom.

entries.title: taken
entries.content:
taken = counselled.

land. Some codices, with three early printed editions and Aramaean, read "inhabitants of the land".

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content:
the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

Behold. Figure of speech Asterismos.

Me. A Massoretic note ( App-30 ) says that this is a cryptogram (Hebrew " Casdim "), meaning "the Chaldees". See note on Jeremiah 51:41 ; Jeremiah 25:26 .

destroying = laying waste. Hebrew. shahath. The same word as in verses: Jeremiah 51:11 , Jeremiah 51:20 , Jeremiah 51:25 . Not the same as in verses: Jeremiah 51:3 , Jeremiah 51:8 , Jeremiah 51:54 , Jer 3:55 .

wind. Hebrew. ruach. App-9 .

entries.title: fanners . . . fan = winnowers . . . winnow.
entries.content: fanners . . . fan = winnowers . . . winnow. Figure of speech Polyptoton. App-6 .

entries.title: Against him that bendeth, &c.
entries.content:
Against him that bendeth, &c. The Massorah ( App-30 ), instead of cancelling the repeated word "against . . . and against" ('el), directs the substitution of 'al, "not . . . and not". The verse will then read, "Let not the archer bend his bow, nor let him lift himself up in his coat of mail" (i.e. in defence of Babylon). This is so read in two early printed editions, Chaldee, Syriac, Vulgate, and Revised Version.

brigandine = coat of mail.

destroy = break down. Hebrew. haram. Same word as Jeremiah 51:54 . Not the same as verses: Jeremiah 51:1 , Jeremiah 51:8 , Jeremiah 51:11 , Jeremiah 51:20 , Jeremiah 51:25 , Jeremiah 51:25 , Jeremiah 51:54 , Jeremiah 51:55 .

entries.title: Israel . . . Judah.
entries.content:
Israel . . . Judah. Now one People again.

God. Hebrew. Elohim. App-4 .

the LORD of Hosts. See note on Jeremiah 6:6 , and 1 Samuel 1:3 .

sin. Hebrew. chata.

the Holy One of Israel. See note on Psalms 71:22 .

entries.title: every man.
entries.content:
every man. Hebrew. 'ish. App-14 .

soul. Hebrew. nephesh. App-13 .

iniquity. Hebrew. 'avah. App-44 . Put by Fig, Metonymy (of Cause), for the judgment brought down by it. Compare Revelation 18:4 .

entries.title: made all the earth drunken.
entries.content:
made all the earth drunken. Compare Revelation 17:4 .

wine. Hebrew. yayin. App-27 .

entries.title: is suddenly, &c.
entries.content:
is suddenly, &c. This must refer to a future fulfilment, for the present condition came gradually, See Isaiah 21:9 ; Isaiah 47:9 , Isaiah 47:11 . Compare Revelation 14:8 ; Revelation 18:8 , Revelation 18:10 , Revelation 18:17 , Revelation 18:19 .

destroyed = broken down. Hebrew. shabar. Not the same as in verses: Jeremiah 51:1 , Jeremiah 51:3 , Jeremiah 51:11 , Jer 1:20 , Jer 1:25 , Jer 1:25 , Jer 1:55 .

take balm = fetch balSamaritan Pentateuch Compare Jeremiah 8:22 ; Jeremiah 46:11 .

entries.title: We.
entries.content:
We. Note this remarkable pronoun.

every one. Hebrew. 'Ish . App-14 .

is lifted up = mounteth.

entries.title: spirit.
entries.content:
spirit. Hebrew. ruach . App-9 .

the Medes. In the person of Cyrus and others ( App-57 ). Here the then immediate calamity is referred to.

vengeance = avengement.

entries.title: make the watch, &c.
entries.content: make the watch, &c. Compare Isaiah 21:5 , Isaiah 21:6 .

entries.title: upon many waters.
entries.content:
upon many waters. Compare Jeremiah 51:42 , and Jeremiah 50:38 , also Revelation 17:1 , Revelation 17:15 .

covetousness = dishonest or unrighteous gain.

entries.title: by Himself
entries.content:
by Himself = by His soul. Hebrew. nephesh. App-13 . Figure of speech Anthropopatheia.

caterpillers = locusts. Compare Joel 2:2 .Nahum 3:15 .

they: i.e. the assailants.

entries.title: made the earth, &c.
entries.content: made the earth, &c. Reference to Pentateuch (Genesis 1 ). Compare Jeremiah 10:12 , &c. verses: Jeremiah 51:15-19 are repeated from Jeremiah 10:12-16 .

entries.title: multitude
entries.content:
multitude = noise.

lightnings, &c. Compare Jeremiah 10:13 .

entries.title: is brutish by, &c.
entries.content:
is brutish by, &c. = is become too brutish to know.

confounded = put to shame.

breath. Hebrew. ruach. App-9 .

entries.title: the time of their visitation.
entries.content: the time of their visitation. See note on Jeremiah 8:12 .

entries.title: The Portion of Jacob, &c.
entries.content: The Portion of Jacob, &c. Note the Alternation in Jeremiah 51:19 , Not such as these is Jacob's Portion: (Deuteronomy 32:9 . Psalms 16:5 ). For [the] Former of all things is He: And the Sceptre of his (Israel's) inheritance: The LORD of hosts is His Name (Deuteronomy 10:9 ).

entries.title: My battle axe:
entries.content:
My battle axe: or, My hammer, i.e. Cyrus. Figure of speech Anthropopatheia.

with thee will I break in pieces = with thee will I beat down. Note the Figure of speech Anaphora , by which ten successive sentences commence with these words, This is for special emphasis.

entries.title: evil.
entries.content:
evil. Hebrew. ra'a'. App-44 .

saith the LORD = [is] Jehovah's oracle.

entries.title: not take of thee . . . forever.
entries.content:
not take of thee . . . forever. This again must refer to a future fulfilment. The two destructions are intertwined. Compare Jeremiah 51:62 .

for ever. See App-151 .

entries.title: prepare
entries.content:
prepare = set apart, or sanctify.

Minni. Frequently mentioned in the inscriptions, the Assyrians having been compelled to quell revolts there.

captain = muster-master or marshal, like the Assyrian dupsarru, or tablet-writer. Hebrew. tiphsar. Occurs only here and Nahum 3:17 .

entries.title: the
entries.content: the Some codices, with three early printed editions, read "and the".

entries.title: without an inhabitant.
entries.content: without an inhabitant. This must be yet future.

entries.title: The mighty men.
entries.content: The mighty men. Hebrew pi. of gibbor. App-14 .

entries.title: post
entries.content:
post = runner.

at one end. Supply the Ellipsis by the word "each", instead of "one" = "at [each] end". This will accord with the history; for Herodotus says the Babylonians retired to the city, and "remained in their holds". Cyrus, having turned the waters of the Euphrates, entered the city, by the bed of the river, at each end (see Herod 1 191). Compare Daniel 5:3 , Daniel 5:4 , Daniel 5:23 , Daniel 5:30 . The Revised Version, "on every quarter", quite misses the point. This passage, therefore, belongs to the past fulfilment; while others still await a future fulfilment.

entries.title: passages
entries.content:
passages = fords.

stopped = seized.

men. Hebrew, plural of 'enosh.

entries.title: the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel.
entries.content: the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel. See note on Jeremiah 7:3 .

entries.title: me.
entries.content: me. Here, and in Jeremiah 51:35 , the Hebrew text reads "us"; but the margin, and some codices, with two early printed editions, read "me", which is followed by the Authorized Version.

entries.title: inhabitant
entries.content:
inhabitant = inhabitress.

upon. Hebrew text reads "against", but a special various reading called Sevir ( App-34 ) has "upon", with some codices, one early printed edition, Aramaean, Septuagint, Syriac, and Vulgate, which are followed by Authorized Version.

entries.title: dry up.
entries.content:
dry up. Referring to the act of Cyrus (by Gobryas). Compare Jeremiah 51:31 , above.

sea = the river Euphrates. So called from its breadth.

entries.title: dragons
entries.content:
dragons = jackals.

without an inhabitant. This carries us on to the future again. Compare 1 Peter 5:13 .

entries.title: yell:
entries.content: yell: or, shake themselves.

entries.title: feasts
entries.content: feasts = banquets.

entries.title: Sheshach.
entries.content: Sheshach. See note on Jeremiah 25:26 .

entries.title: no man dwelleth.
entries.content:
no man dwelleth. Still future.

man. Hebrew. 'adam. App-14 .

entries.title: the wall of Babylon.
entries.content: the wall of Babylon. Now recently laid bare by excavations.

entries.title: do judgment upon
entries.content: do judgment upon = visit upon.

entries.title: the heaven . . . shall sing.
entries.content:
the heaven . . . shall sing. Figure of speech Poeanismos and Prosopopoeia.

all that is therein. Compare Revelation 19:1-3 .

entries.title: all the earth.
entries.content: all the earth. Compare Isaiah 14:16 , Isaiah 14:17 .

entries.title: the LORD.
entries.content: the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. (with 'eth). App-4 .

entries.title: mount up, &c.
entries.content: mount up, &c. Compare Isaiah 14:12-15 .

entries.title: destroyed
entries.content: destroyed = caused to perish. Hebrew. 'abar. Not the same as in verses: Jeremiah 51:1 , Jeremiah 51:3 , Jeremiah 51:8 , Jeremiah 1:11 , Jer 1:20 , Jer 1:25 , Jer 1:54 .

entries.title: GOD.
entries.content: GOD. Hebrew El. App-4 . The Hebrew reads "El of recompences, Jehovah".

entries.title: walls.
entries.content:
walls. Some codices, with two early printed editions, Septuagint, and Vulgate, read "wall".

people = peoples.

be weary = faint.

entries.title: The Fifty-First Prophecy of Jeremiah
entries.content:
The Fifty-First Prophecy of Jeremiah (see book comments for Jeremiah).

Seraiah. The brother of Baruch(Jeremiah 32:12 . Compare Jeremiah 45:1 ).

when he went, &c. Probably to renew his oath of allegiance. Compare Jeremiah 27:1 ; Jeremiah 28:1 .

quiet prince. Probably chief chamberlain. Revised Version margin, "quartermaster. "Hebrew = quiet resting-place (Isaiah 32:18 ). Probably his office was to prepare the night's camping place during the journey to Babylon.

entries.title: wrote in a book
entries.content:
wrote in a book = wrote in one scroll.

evil = calamity. Hebrew. ra'a . App-44 .

entries.title: and shalt see, &c.
entries.content: and shalt see, &c. = then shalt thou look out and read.

entries.title: desolate for ever
entries.content: desolate for ever = age-abiding desolations, show-ing that this prophecy must wait a future fulfilment.

entries.title: Zedekiah.
entries.content: Zedekiah. Compare 2 Kings 24:18-20 . Reigned from 489 to 477 B.C.

entries.title: evil.
entries.content:
evil. Hebrew. ra'a'. App-44 .

the LORD. Hebrew. Jehovah. App-4 .

entries.title: ninth year.
entries.content: ninth year. Compare 2 Kings 25:1-21 .

entries.title: the famine.
entries.content: the famine. Described in the Lamentations of Jeremiah. See note on Genesis 12:10 .

entries.title: fled, &c.
entries.content:
fled, &c. Compare 2 Kings 25:4 .

between the two walls . . . king's garden. See App-68 .

entries.title: Biblah.
entries.content: Biblah. Now Ribleh. On the east bank of the Greekntes, thirty-five miles north-east of Baalbek.

entries.title: put out the eyes.
entries.content: put out the eyes. See note on Jeremiah 32:4 . Compare 2 Kings 25:6 , 2 Kings 25:7 . Ezekiel 12:13 . Hence, Zedekiah never saw Babylon, though he was taken thither.

entries.title: tenth day.
entries.content:
tenth day. In 2 Kings 25:8 it says "seventh day", but that was "[to] Jerusalem". This is "into Jerusalem".

into = in.

entries.title: the poor of the people.
entries.content: the poor of the people. This is supplemental to 2 Kings 25:12 . Hebrew. dal = impoverished. See note on "poverty", Proverbs 6:11 . Compare Nehemiah 1:3 .

entries.title: pillars of brass.
entries.content: pillars of brass. Compare Jeremiah 27:19 .

entries.title: the shovels, &c.
entries.content:
the shovels, &c. Reference to Pentateuch (Exodus 27:3 , &c).

bowls = bowls for sprinkling.

entries.title: firepans
entries.content:
firepans = censers.

candlesticks = lamps.

entries.title: under
entries.content: under = beneath.

entries.title: pillars.
entries.content:
pillars. Compare 1 Kings 7:15 . 2 Kings 25:17 .

cubits. See App-51 .

entries.title: chapiter
entries.content: chapiter = capital.

entries.title: ninety and six.
entries.content:
ninety and six. There were 100 "round about"; Compare 2 Chronicles 3:16 ; 2 Chronicles 4:13 ; with 1 Kings 7:20 .

on a side. Hebrew. ruach. See App-9 . = towards the air, or open air. The other four being behind, out of sight.

entries.title: Seraiah.
entries.content:
Seraiah. See 2 Kings 25:18 . 1 Chronicles 6:14 . Compare Jeremiah 51:59 .

door = threshold.

entries.title: seven.
entries.content: seven. In 2 Kings 25:19 "five"; but the greater includes the lesser.

entries.title: land
entries.content: land = soil.

entries.title: the seventh year.
entries.content: the seventh year. This was at the beginning of Nebuchadrezzar's second siege, the year before Jehoiachin's captivity, 490 B.C.

entries.title: the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar
entries.content:
the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar was the second year of his third and last siege, or 478 B.C.

persons = souls. Hebrew. nephesh.

entries.title: three and twentieth year.
entries.content: three and twentieth year. Four years after the fall of Jerusalem. Another contact of Bible and secular chronology, 473 B.C. See App-86 .

entries.title: seven and thirtieth year.
entries.content:
seven and thirtieth year. Compare 2 Kings 25:27-30 . See App-50 .

Jehoiachin. Elsewhere in this book called "Jeconiah" (Jeremiah 24:1 ; Jeremiah 29:2 ), or "Coniah" (Jeremiah 22:24 , Jeremiah 22:28 ).
